acceptedClaims.declaredStatement: Assume the Geng--Jog--Nair--Wang theorem that Marton's private-message sum-rate for every binary-input broadcast channel equals randomized time division. For the half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, every finite Marton law whose induced super-input X_1X_2 is supported on at most two of {00,01,10,11} has sum-rate strictly below 0.615 bits. Consequently, because the product randomized-time-division value is greater than 0.7232857688439092 bits, every strict two-letter Marton improvement over the current BSSC achievable rate must use at least three super-input symbols. This is only a support-pruning result and does not rule out a gain on three- or four-symbol support.
acceptedClaims.validitySummary: Conditional on the explicitly assumed binary-input Marton-equals-randomized-time-division theorem, the argument exhausts all supports of size at most two. Adjacent and antirepetition supports admit cooperative BEC(1/2) converses, while the repetition support is bounded via the assumed theorem and a rigorous concavity/interval calculation by 0.614336840676774 bits, hence strictly below 0.615. Since the stated product RTD baseline exceeds 0.7232857688439092 bits, any strict two-letter improvement must use at least three super-input symbols.
scopeQualifications: The numerical product RTD benchmark is treated as supplied problem data; the execution attestation does not independently prove it.
The result only excludes supports of cardinality at most two and makes no assertion against gains using three- or four-symbol support.
Validity is conditional on the Geng–Jog–Nair–Wang theorem explicitly assumed in the claim.
